stem_en: A code-review prompt already lists explicit report/skip categories, yet it keeps missing injection vulnerabilities inside ORM query builders while reporting them correctly in raw SQL strings. What addition improves recall without adding noise?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Add a "be thorough, miss nothing" instruction to the prompt so that the reviewer widens its search across every place a query is built.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Raise the model's reasoning effort so that it spends longer analyzing each place where a query is assembled.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Add a concrete code example for the security category showing the injection pattern inside an ORM builder, not only in raw SQL.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Ask the model to rate its confidence on each finding and lower the reporting threshold so borderline cases surface.

explanation_ja: 明示的なカテゴリに加え、各重大度・各カテゴリに具体的なコード例を付けるのが精度改善の定石である。見逃しているパターンをそのまま例として示せば、カテゴリの解釈が広がる。よって C。A は曖昧な語の追加で効かない。B は基準が無いまま考えても検出対象は増えない。D は閾値を下げると誤検知も増える。

stem_en: A log-anomaly reporter has two categories: "latency spike" findings are wrong about 80% of the time, while "auth failure" findings are almost always right. On-call engineers have started ignoring the whole report. What is the pragmatic response?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Temporarily disable the latency-spike category while its criteria are improved, so the accurate category keeps its credibility.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Keep both categories but add a disclaimer that latency findings may be wrong, so on-call engineers can weigh them accordingly.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Lower the reporting threshold for auth failures so that more of them appear and outweigh the noisy latency findings.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Merge the two categories into a single "anomaly" category, so engineers triage one list instead of judging per category.

explanation_ja: 高誤検知のカテゴリは正確なカテゴリへの信頼まで損なうため、改善が済むまで無効化する運用が現実的である。よって A。B は免責文を付けても誤検知は届き続け、無視される流れは変わらない。C は正しいカテゴリの精度を落とす。D は誤検知を正確な所見に混ぜて全体を汚す。

stem_en: A translation-QA prompt has detailed instructions, yet its findings vary in format from run to run and the severity assigned to the same kind of error wavers. What is the next technique to apply?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Shorten the instructions so the model has less to misread, leaving only the rules that matter most for severity.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Add a system prompt line saying "be consistent", so the model holds one output format and one severity bar across runs.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Switch to a lower temperature, which cuts sampling variation and should let the format settle down across runs.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Add two to four few-shot examples that demonstrate the exact output format and show why each severity was assigned.

explanation_ja: 詳細な指示だけで出力が安定しないときは few-shot prompting の出番である。形式を実演し、判断理由(なぜその重大度か)を示す例を 2〜4 個入れる。よって D。A は必要な指示を削る。B は曖昧な指示の追加で効果が薄い。C は乱数の影響は減らせても、形式や基準の定義不足は解消しない。

stem_en: A resume-screening prompt flags every employment gap as a concern, including documented parental leave and sabbaticals the company explicitly accepts. Which few-shot design fixes this?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Examples drawn only from flagged resumes (each labeled with the concern it raised), so the model learns what a real concern looks like.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Contrastive pairs: an accepted gap (documented leave) labeled acceptable next to an unexplained multi-year gap labeled a concern.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Examples drawn from a single job family — one consistent role type — so the labeling stays uniform across resumes.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: A list of adjectives describing a strong candidate, such as "stable" and "committed", for the model to match resumes against.

explanation_ja: 誤検知を減らすには、許容パターンと真の問題を対比する例が効く。容認済みの休職を「問題なし」、説明の無い長期空白を「懸念」として並べて示す。よって B。A は問題側の例だけでは境界が学べない。C は多様性を欠き、他の職種に一般化しない。D は形容詞の羅列で判断基準にならない。

stem_en: An extraction pipeline defines a tool with a JSON Schema for its input. Which guarantee does enabling strict tool use add that the plain tool definition lacks?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The extracted values will be semantically correct — totals, dates, and names will agree with the source document.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: The tool inputs will conform to the schema: correct types, required fields present, and no undeclared fields.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The model will always call the tool instead of answering in text, so the pipeline never receives a prose reply.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The tool will be executed server-side by the API, so the pipeline does not have to run the function itself.

explanation_ja: strict tool use はモデルが生成するツール入力がスキーマに準拠することを保証し、構文・型の誤りを排除する。よって B。A は意味エラー(合計不一致など)はスキーマの保証範囲外である。C はツール呼び出しの有無を決めるのは tool_choice であり、strict ではない。D は実行場所と無関係である。

stem_en: A medical-claims pipeline defines three extraction tools — claim form, explanation of benefits, referral — and documents arrive unlabeled. Every document must be handled through a tool call rather than a prose answer, with the model choosing the schema that fits. Which tool_choice is appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: {"type": "any"}: a tool call is guaranteed, and the model picks the schema that fits the document in front of it.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: {"type": "auto"}: the model decides whether a tool is needed, which keeps a prose answer available for odd documents.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: {"type": "tool", "name": "claim_form"}: always start with the most common type and re-route the others afterwards.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: {"type": "none"}: parse the model's text answer, which keeps the three schemas as documentation for reviewers.

explanation_ja: 文書種別が不明で複数スキーマがあるときは any を使い、ツール呼び出し(1 つ以上)を保証しつつ選択はモデルに任せる。厳密に 1 回だけに制限したい場合は disable_parallel_tool_use を併用するが、本問の要件は「散文ではなくツールで処理する」ことなので any で足りる。よって A。B の auto はテキストで答えてしまう可能性が残る。C は請求書以外の文書を無理に請求書スキーマへ押し込む。D は構造化の保証を放棄している。

stem_en: An insurance-claim schema defines claim_type as an enum of five values. Unusual claims are forced into the nearest value, and reviewers later find them misclassified. What schema change is recommended?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Remove the enum and accept any string, so unusual claim types are recorded exactly as they appear in the document.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Add the observed unusual types to the enum, extending it until it covers every claim type reviewers have reported.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Make claim_type optional so the model can leave unusual cases blank whenever none of the five enum values fits.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Add an escape value such as "other" plus a free-text detail field, so unusual cases are flagged explicitly.

explanation_ja: enum に逃げ道が無いと、当てはまらないケースが最寄りの値に押し込まれる。other や unclear + detail のような escape 値を用意し、想定外を明示的に報告させる。よって D。A は正規化の利点を捨てる。B は網羅を目指しても新しい例外は必ず現れる。C は情報自体が失われ、後工程で分類できない。

stem_en: An order-extraction schema validates perfectly, yet reviewers find records where the billing address was placed in the shipping_address field and vice versa. The team asks why the schema did not catch it and what will. Which answer is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The schema was missing a required flag on shipping_address; adding that flag will make a swapped record fail validation on arrival.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Field swaps are a syntax error that a plain tool definition lets through, so enabling strict mode will reject them.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Schemas guarantee structure, not meaning; add application-side cross-field checks and few-shot examples showing where each address goes.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Increase max_tokens so the model has room to finish placing both addresses in the fields they belong to.

explanation_ja: フィールドの取り違えは値が型・構造に適合したまま意味だけが誤る意味エラーで、スキーマや strict mode では防げない。アプリ側の検証ルールと、配置を示す few-shot 例で対処する。よって C。A と B はスキーマの保証範囲を誤解している。D はトークン数の問題ではない。

stem_en: An extraction retry loop resends only the original document with the message "Try again" whenever validation fails. Retries rarely succeed. What should the retry request include?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The original document, the failed extraction, and the specific validation error, so the model knows what to fix.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: A higher temperature, so the second attempt samples differently from the first instead of repeating the same output.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Only the validation error message, keeping the request short so retries stay cheap at this volume of documents.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: A different document from the same batch, so throughput holds up while the failed one waits in the queue.

explanation_ja: 再試行が効くのは、元文書・失敗した抽出・具体的な検証エラーを併せて渡し、何を直すべきかを伝えたときである。よって A。B はランダムに変えるだけで、誤りの修正にはならない。C は文書が無ければ正しい値を再抽出できない。D は問題を別の入力にすり替えている。

stem_en: Some purchase orders show one total in the header and a different one on the summary page. The pipeline silently returns whichever it saw first, and reviewers cannot tell such documents apart from clean ones. Which schema addition helps the validation loop?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: A confidence score for the whole document, so documents the model is unsure about can be routed to a reviewer.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: A conflict_detected field listing both values and where each appeared, so those documents can be routed for review.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: A boolean is_valid field that the model sets, so the loop can pass through only the documents it marks valid.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: A free-text notes field where the model records anything unusual it noticed, so reviewers can read it during triage.

explanation_ja: 矛盾するソース値を検知するには、conflict_detected のようなフィールドで両方の値と出所を返させ、検証ループが該当文書を振り分けられるようにする。よって B。A は文書全体の確信度では矛盾の有無が分からない。C はモデル自身の妥当性判断で、較正されておらず信頼できない。D は機械的に処理できない。

stem_en: A retailer has two jobs: (1) classify two million historical product reviews with no deadline, and (2) generate a reply suggestion while a support agent is chatting with a customer. How should the Message Batches API be used?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Use it for both jobs, since the 50% discount applies to every request regardless of how urgent that request is.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Use it for the live chat job only (replies are short, so a batch of them should come back quickly) and the synchronous API for the backlog.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Use it for the historical classification (50% cheaper, non-blocking) and the synchronous API for the live chat.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Avoid it entirely, because a workload with no latency SLA cannot be depended on by either of these two jobs.

explanation_ja: Batches API は 50% のコスト減と引き換えに最大 24 時間の処理窓でレイテンシ SLA が無い。締切の無い大量処理には最適で、対話中の応答生成には不向きである。よって C。A は対話が待てない。B は逆の割り当て。D は SLA が無いことは非同期処理にとって問題ではない。

stem_en: A 60,000-document batch — one request per document — returns results in an order unrelated to submission, and the team cannot reliably match each result to its source record. Roughly 1% of requests fail and must be re-run. What mechanism solves both problems?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Submit one request per batch, so results come back in submission order and any failure is isolated to one batch.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Sort the results by their timestamp — that restores the submission order and lets them be zipped back to the records.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Embed the record ID in the prompt text and parse it back out of the model's answer as the results are read.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Assign a custom_id to each request: it maps results back to records, and failed requests can be resubmitted alone.

explanation_ja: custom_id は各リクエストに付ける識別子で、結果の突合と失敗分だけの再提出の両方に使える。よって D。A は Batches の利点を失う。B はタイムスタンプで元レコードは特定できない。C は出力の文言に依存し、失敗した結果には出力自体が無い。

stem_en: To get an independent review, a pipeline appends "Now switch roles: you are a strict reviewer. Critique the findings above." to the same session that produced the findings. Almost nothing gets revised. Why, and what works instead?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The switch leaves the session's own reasoning context in place, so it still rarely doubts itself; send the artifact to a context-free instance.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: The reviewer persona needs a longer prompt that describes how strict to be and which standards it should apply to each finding.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Extended thinking must be enabled for role switching to work; without it the reviewer persona reasons no differently.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Reviews are unnecessary once the generator has used few-shot examples, which already rule out the failure modes.

explanation_ja: 同じセッションはペルソナを変えても生成時の推論文脈を持ち続け、自分の判断を疑いにくい。文脈を持たない第二インスタンスに成果物だけを渡すのが有効である。よって A。B と C は同一セッションの限界を prompt や思考量で補おうとしており、根本原因が残る。D は品質保証を放棄している。

stem_en: A multi-pass reviewer produces solid and shaky findings alike, and the team wants to auto-post only the reliable ones while sending the rest to a human. What should the pipeline add?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: A rule that posts only the first ten findings, on the assumption that the reviewer reports its strongest ones first.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Per-finding self-reported confidence, calibrated on labeled examples, to route findings to auto-post or human review.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: A second identical pass whose findings replace the first, so the later and more considered set is what gets posted.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: A longer prompt that repeats the request to be careful before posting any finding, without adding a measurable reliability signal.

explanation_ja: 所見ごとの自己申告 confidence を labeled set で較正し、閾値で自動投稿と人間レビューに振り分けるのが推奨パターンである。よって B。A は件数と信頼性は無関係。C は同じ設定の再実行で信頼度の情報は増えない。D は曖昧な指示で精度は変わらない。
